themes.consensus_view: Most banks agree the AI spending boom is still going strong, but money is rotating out of the big cloud companies doing the spending and into the chip and memory makers selling them the gear, with the open question being whether all that spending ever shows up as real revenue.

facts_agreed.claim: The AI investment boom is still intact and a major driver of growth and earnings.
evidence_quotes: vast majority of AI demand indicators we are tracking continue to point to robust demand
its not the end, we remain in the midst of a historic investment boom
AI investment boom is an engine of global growth at the moment
This almost secular growth driver is likely to continue to underpin AI-related sectors.
Forecasts anticipate unprecedented YoY growth in 2026 of 64%

facts_agreed.claim: Capital is rotating away from the hyperscalers that spend on AI toward the semiconductor and infrastructure suppliers that benefit from the spending.
evidence_quotes: The market has rewarded the providers (i.e Semis companies) instead of the spenders (Hyperscalers).
it feels like a continuation of funding trade with money rotating into semis and memory
Hyperscalers then evolving as the funding Shorts over the past few quarters
beneficiaries of the Capex spigots being opened full throttle into the 'AI Enablers'
pricing beneficiaries of these bottlenecks to continue to outperform

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure stocks, concentrated in a few memory and chip names, are driving a large share of S&P 500 earnings growth.
evidence_quotes: AI infrastructure stocks are expected to contribute nearly 60% of S&P 500 EPS growth

facts_contested.claim: Whether the trillions in AI capex are sustainable and will earn a return
facts_contested.for_evidence: AI infrastructure spending remains alive and well despite the growing debate
facts_contested.against_evidence: there remains a searing debate within the market on the sustainability of trillions of dollars

facts_contested.claim: Whether the tech sector rotation is a healthy reallocation or a risk-off exit
facts_contested.for_evidence: combined % net selling across the two sectors was the largest in over 10 years
facts_contested.against_evidence: US stocks were mostly lower this week driven by underperformance in Tech

themes.consensus_view: Banks across roughly 17 desks reference Strait of Hormuz transit and security as a live oil-supply story, tracking the disruption and the gradual restart of Gulf shipping, but none has staked a clear directional view on where it resolves.

facts_agreed.claim: Many banks flag the Strait of Hormuz as a key oil chokepoint where shipping was disrupted and is now in the process of recovering.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz oil flow disruption

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks frame the strait as a maritime-security and transit-safety concern still being worked through, including de-mining and vessel-transit threats.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz maritime security risks
Strait of Hormuz vessel transit threats

themes.consensus_view: Banks across many desks reference Kevin Warsh's Fed chairmanship and how he runs press conferences and signals policy as a near-term thing to watch, but nobody has staked a directional view on what it means for rates.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag Kevin Warsh's Fed chairmanship and his communication style as a live focus this window.
evidence_quotes: Fed communications regime under Chairman Warsh
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh inflation target commitment
Chair Kevin Warsh Fed leadership style

themes.consensus_view: Banks across eight desks flag a US-Iran peace deal or memorandum of understanding as a live near-term catalyst, but none has staked out a clear directional view on whether it holds or how to trade it.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks are tracking US-Iran peace negotiations and a possible ceasefire or memorandum of understanding as an active catalyst this window.
A US-Iran deal is framed as enabling Iran's reintegration into the global economy, with reconstruction financing in view.
